hypothesis: Single-order buyers churn more than repeat buyers
business_meaning: Supported. A single-order buyer is ~6x more likely (odds) to churn: the second order is the key retention moment.

hypothesis: Buyers who remove more items from cart churn more
result: Median removal rate 0.350 (churned) vs 0.467 (retained), n=71,568; stratified single-order: r=-0.143 (p=2.6e-70); repeat: r=-0.057 (p=3.9e-08)
business_meaning: Rejected as stated: churners remove LESS. Cart removal signals active comparison shopping by engaged users, so it should not trigger churn alerts.

hypothesis: December (holiday) acquired buyers retain worse than November acquired
test: Two-proportion z-test on 'no 2nd order within 60 days of first order' (recency-free)
result: No 2nd order within 60 days: 84.41% (Dec-acquired, n=19,702) vs 80.43% (Nov-acquired, n=26,761); diff 3.98 pp [CI 3.29, 4.68]; RR 1.049. Raw Jan-Feb churn diff 1.71 pp
business_meaning: Statistically supported but practically small (negligible effect size): holiday-acquired buyers are slightly less likely to come back within 60 days. Worth a tailored post-holiday second-order offer, but it is not the main churn driver.

hypothesis: Buyers with no site activity in the last 31 days churn more
test: Chi-square (3 engagement groups x churn) + two-proportion z-test (none vs any)
result: Churn 92.93% (no activity, n=35,810) vs 77.24% (any activity); diff 15.69 pp [CI 15.18, 16.20]; OR 3.87
business_meaning: Supported: silence is the warning sign. Trigger re-engagement after ~30 days without a visit, rather than on a dip in activity.

hypothesis: Churners had lower average order value than retained buyers
business_meaning: Statistically real but small: basket size alone is a weak churn signal, so the model needs behaviour (orders, recency, activity), not just spend.

hypothesis: First-order basket value differs by acquisition month (Oct*/Nov/Dec)
result: Median first-order value Oct 29.99, Nov 28.92, Dec 24.47; pairwise: Oct vs Nov r=0.020; Oct vs Dec r=0.108; Nov vs Dec r=0.088
business_meaning: Differences exist but are tiny: December buyers do not start with much smaller baskets, so their weaker retention comes from behaviour after the first order.
